ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, point O is the origin, point A $(-3,0)$ and point B $(0,2)$ are both on the coordinate axes. If the graph of the inverse proportion function $y= \frac{k}{x}$ passes through the center of symmetry of rectangle AOBC, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[
\text{Solution:} \quad \because \text{Point A} (-3, 0) \text{ and Point B} (0, 2) \text{ are both on the coordinate axes}, \\
\therefore \text{the center of rectangle AOBC is} \left( -\frac{3}{2} ,1\right), \\
\because \text{the graph of the inverse proportion function } y= \frac{k}{x} \text{ passes through the center of symmetry of rectangle AOBC}, \\
\therefore k= -\frac{3}{2} \times 1 = \boxed{-\frac{3}{2}}
\]
